logp.method_description: After mixing octanol and purified water in a 15-mL centrifuge tube, the mixture was shaken in a constant temperature shaker at 37°C for 24 h to achieve mutual saturation of the two phases, preparing saturated solutions of both phases. After allowing the solution to settle for 1 h, it was separated and kept aside. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated octanol to obtain solutions of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM concentrations. UV/Vis absorbance measurements were used to construct a standard curve. Subsequently, using the octanol-saturated solution prepared earlier as the solvent, a 50 μM test sample was prepared. An equal volume of water-saturated solution was added, and the mixture was oscillated at 37°C for 48 h. Afterward, the mixed solution was centrifuged at 2500 rpm for 15 min to separate the two phases. The absorbance of the octanol solution was measured using a UV spectrophotometer, and the drug's concentration in the octanol phase (Co) was calculated using the standard curve. According to the principle of mass conservation, the concentration in the water phase (Cw) was determined, and log Po/w was calculated by Formula (1). Log Po/w = log(Co/Cw)
